text: Chapter 11 says naming is not labelling something you already built. What is the alternative claim?
choices: That names are for the compiler's benefit, so any consistent scheme works equally well.
That choosing the name is how you decide what the method should be, so the name comes first and constrains the body.
That names should be chosen after the implementation, when its behaviour is known.
That a good name makes documentation unnecessary, so naming replaces comments.
explanation: If you can name it, you know what it does; if you cannot, you have not decided. That is why a comment labelling a section of a long method is Chapter 14's signal that a method is waiting to be extracted — the comment is a name looking for a home. The practical test is whether the name is a promise you could keep while replacing the body entirely.
